info.title: Webhooks HTTP Endpoint
info.description:
Manage webhooks for your projects.

## Types
Sanity provides two types of webhooks, transaction and document. Document webhooks are preferred because they are more flexible and powerful.

### Document webhooks
A document webhook triggers every time a document is created, updated, or deleted. If a transaction updates three documents, three webhooks are executed. Document webhooks also allow for more granular filtering and customizable payloads with GROQ.

### Transaction webhooks
A transaction webhook triggers once per dataset, meaning if you batch together multiple document mutations in one transaction, only one webhook is executed.

401.description: Missing or invalid token, or the token lacks the required webhooks grant. For example, `User must have grant sanity.project.webhooks/read to perform this operation`.

400.description: Bad request. For example, `Hostname not allowed` when the URL resolves to a private address, `Hostname not resolvable: <hostname>` when the URL's hostname can't be resolved, or `You have used all the included webhooks in your plan. In order to add more webhooks, you need to upgrade your plan.` when the project has reached its document webhook quota.

schema.description: Fields to update. Fields you leave out keep their current values. Transaction webhooks created with `type: transaction` reject `apiVersion`, `includeDrafts`, `includeAllVersions`, `headers`, and `secret` with the error `Invalid fields specified for transaction hook`. `rule` and `httpMethod` are accepted for transaction webhooks but have no effect.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the webhook was created

createdByUserId.description: ID of the user who created the webhook

isDisabled.description: Whether the webhook is currently disabled

deletedAt.description: Timestamp when the webhook was deleted, if applicable

filter.description: Legacy per-event filter object. Use `rule.filter` instead.

projection.description: Legacy per-event projection object. Use `rule.projection` instead.

url.description: The endpoint to which the webhook request is sent. Must start with `http://` or `https://`, and must not resolve to a private address.

dataset.description: Which dataset should this trigger for. Use a dataset name (letters, numbers, `_`, and `-`, stored lowercase), or `*` for all datasets in the project.

description.description: Optional description to add helpful context to the webhook

rule.description: Configuration for when and how the webhook should trigger

on.description: Webhooks can be triggered when a document is created, updated, deleted, or any combination of these

filter.description: A GROQ filter specifying which documents will, when changed, trigger your webhook. A filter is what you commonly see between the `*[` and `]` in a GROQ query. This field supports all the GROQ functions you'd expect and has additional support for functions in the delta:: namespace, as well as before() and after(). If left empty, it will apply to all documents (`*[]`)

projection.description: A GROQ projection defining the payload (or body) of the outgoing webhook request. This field supports GROQ functions in the delta:: namespace, as well as before() and after(). If left empty, it will include the whole document after the change that triggered it

apiVersion.description: Which API version to use for the GROQ filter and projection. Use the format `vYYYY-MM-DD`, or `vX`.

httpMethod.description: This field configures the webhook's HTTP request method. It can be set to POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, or GET. Some endpoints require incoming requests to use a specific method to work

includeDrafts.description: Set to trigger on changes to draft documents.

includeAllVersions.description: Set to trigger on changes to version documents.

headers.description: Additional HTTP headers. You can add multiple headers. A common example is adding an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header to authenticate the webhook request. The total size of all headers can not exceed 2 kB. Header names can only contain letters, numbers, and hyphens, and values must be ASCII without line breaks. The `content-length`, `connection`, `keep-alive`, `proxy-authenticate`, `proxy-authorization`, `te`, `trailer`, `transfer-encoding`, and `upgrade` headers are not allowed.

secret.description: To let receiving services verify the origin of any outgoing webhook, you may add a secret that will be hashed and included as part of the webhook request's headers

isDisabledByUser.description: Set to 'true' to disable the webhook and prevent it from triggering

type.description: Set to 'transaction', or omit. Requests without a type create a transaction webhook.

url.description: The endpoint to which the webhook request is sent. Must start with `http://` or `https://`, and must not resolve to a private address.

dataset.description: Which dataset should this trigger for. Use a dataset name (letters, numbers, `_`, and `-`, stored lowercase), or `*` for all datasets in the project.
